title: 2003 AMC 10A Problem 10
statement: The polygon enclosed by the solid lines in the figure consists of \(4\) congruent squares joined edge-to-edge. One more congruent square is attached to an edge at one of the nine positions indicated. How many of the nine resulting polygons can be folded to form a cube with one face missing?

solutions.text:
Fold the four shaded squares first. They occupy four distinct faces of the cube, leaving two faces open.

Checking the numbered attachments, positions \(1,\) \(2,\) and \(3\) fold the new square onto a face already occupied by one of the shaded squares. Positions \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) \(7,\) \(8,\) and \(9\) fold it onto one of the two open faces. Therefore exactly \(6\) of the \(9\) polygons work.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The four squares already wrap into four side faces of a cube
The fifth square must fold up as one of the two remaining faces without landing on a face already covered
